definition: An ownership interest in an exchange-listed company.
reading: The price describes the value of one share in the listing currency.
pitfalls: The price can fall and dividends are not guaranteed.

definition: The distribution of portfolio value along a selected dimension.
reading: Weights refer to the same valuation basis.
pitfalls: An ETF's listing currency does not describe all currencies of its assets.

definition: A smoothed measure of the price range that accounts for gaps.
reading: The value is expressed in the instrument's price units.
pitfalls: It does not specify direction or the maximum possible loss.

definition: A price average surrounded by bands based on historical volatility.
reading: The period and multiplier determine band width.
pitfalls: The band is not a range of guaranteed future prices.

definition: An index or ETF used as a reference.
reading: Comparison requires matching periods and currencies.
pitfalls: Differences in composition and costs limit comparability.

definition: The price of one instrument unit in its listing currency.
reading: Check the quote's source, time and delay.
pitfalls: The price is neither the value of the whole position nor a guaranteed execution price.

definition: A contract settling the difference in an instrument's price.
reading: It does not represent share ownership. OligInvest does not model CFD positions.
pitfalls: Leverage increases both potential gains and losses.

definition: A distribution of some of a company's funds to its shareholders.
reading: Gross amount, withheld tax and net amount have different meanings.
pitfalls: A historical dividend does not imply an identical future payment.

definition: The part of a foreign position's P/L associated with changes in the instrument price.
reading: Together with the currency effect, it forms PLN P/L under the calculation definition.
pitfalls: It depends on lot and exchange-rate data; it is not a separate rate of return.

definition: The part of a foreign position's P/L associated with changes in exchange rates.
reading: It complements the price effect to form PLN P/L.
pitfalls: The historical effect does not determine future exchange-rate direction.

definition: An average giving more weight to recent prices.
reading: The period determines how quickly it responds to price changes.
pitfalls: The result depends on warmup and the chosen start of history.

definition: Data available after a trading session ends.
reading: The session date identifies the close it relates to.
pitfalls: It is not a current executable transaction price.

definition: A fund whose units are traded on an exchange.
reading: The fund name and documents describe the market it tracks.
pitfalls: The listing currency does not describe the fund's entire currency risk.

definition: The account's cash balance, with its currency specified.
reading: The base-currency balance uses the exchange rate applied in the valuation.
pitfalls: Missing history or exchange rates can prevent full balance reconciliation.

definition: The Warsaw Stock Exchange.
reading: MIC XWAR identifies the market.
pitfalls: A calendar day is not always a trading day.

definition: The number of instrument units in a transaction, position or lot.
reading: The initial quantity describes the lot at opening; the remaining quantity accounts for consumption so far.
pitfalls: A split changes unit count and unit cost, but does not itself change total cost.

definition: A measure of the value of a specified basket of instruments.
reading: An index change describes the change in that basket.
pitfalls: An index and a fund tracking it can have different performance and costs.

definition: A permanent instrument identifier in OligInvest.
reading: It links quotes and transactions for the same instrument.
pitfalls: A symbol change does not necessarily mean a different instrument.

definition: A 12-character international securities identifier.
reading: It helps identify an instrument independently of its name.
pitfalls: ISIN alone does not identify the listing market.

definition: The market value of all shares in a company.
reading: It combines the share price with the number of shares.
pitfalls: It is not the amount of cash held by the company.

definition: The cost of remaining units divided by their quantity.
reading: This is an informational average-cost view; lot matching uses FIFO per account.
pitfalls: Missing acquisition cost means missing data, not zero cost.

definition: The cost assigned to held units under the accounting rules.
reading: FIFO assigns disposals to the oldest lots in the account.
pitfalls: An unknown cost is not a zero cost.

definition: A historical price adjusted for events such as splits.
reading: Indicators use split-adjusted prices.
pitfalls: An adjusted price is not the actual settlement price of a transaction.

definition: The difference between two exponential averages and its smoothing.
reading: The histogram shows the difference between the MACD line and its smoothing.
pitfalls: Crossovers describe historical data and can frequently reverse direction.

definition: A code identifying the listing market.
reading: XWAR, XNYS and XNAS represent different markets.
pitfalls: The same instrument can be listed on more than one market.

definition: An alternative trading system operated by GPW.
reading: It is a separate market segment.
pitfalls: Lower turnover can make execution at the displayed price difficult.

definition: The value of transactions during a period.
reading: It always has a monetary unit.
pitfalls: It differs from the number of units, known as volume.

definition: Open, high, low and close prices, and volume, for one interval.
reading: The candle shows the price range and change; volume is a separate measure.
pitfalls: Daily data does not show the sequence of events within a session.

definition: Quotes displayed some time after they were recorded.
reading: The label gives the time, source and declared delay.
pitfalls: Source delay and stale data after an outage are different things.

definition: The difference between value and cost in the selected view.
reading: A positive sign means a gain and a negative sign a loss in that view.
pitfalls: Economic and tax results may differ.

definition: A fee charged for executing a transaction.
reading: P/L after costs includes this fee.
pitfalls: No commission does not mean no spread or currency costs.

definition: Exchanging one currency for another.
reading: PLN P/L also depends on the exchange rate.
pitfalls: The broker's rate may differ from NBP's average rate.

definition: The amount received from the transactions being accounted for, under the selected view.
reading: Proceeds and costs must cover the same complete set of transactions.
pitfalls: Proceeds alone are not profit; account for cost and disclosed data exclusions.

definition: A brokerage account represented in the Application.
reading: Each account has a currency and type.
pitfalls: FIFO lots are matched separately for each account.

definition: A measure of the relationship between historical price gains and losses.
reading: The value lies on a scale from 0 to 100.
pitfalls: The RSI level alone does not determine future price direction.

definition: The period during which a market conducts trading.
reading: Chart dates follow the exchange calendar.
pitfalls: Holidays and time zones differ across exchanges.

definition: The average closing price over a selected number of intervals.
reading: A longer period smooths short-term changes more strongly.
pitfalls: Smoothing delays the response; the start of the series lacks a full window.

definition: A change in share count and unit price caused by splitting or combining shares.
reading: A split itself does not change the position's value.
pitfalls: Unadjusted history can appear to contain a sudden price jump.

definition: The difference between prices on the two sides of the order book.
reading: It is one component of transaction execution cost.
pitfalls: The last traded price may not currently be available.

definition: An index containing companies from a selected sector.
reading: It helps describe changes in one part of the market.
pitfalls: Sector classification does not describe all sources of a company's revenue.

definition: A graphical record of an interval's open, close and extreme prices.
reading: The body shows the change and the wicks show the price range.
pitfalls: A candle's shape alone does not determine future price changes.

definition: An abbreviation identifying an instrument.
reading: Search maps provider symbols to the instrument in the Application.
pitfalls: The same abbreviation can identify different instruments.

definition: A rate of return that neutralizes external deposits and withdrawals.
reading: It enables comparison of value changes over time without the effect of contribution size.
pitfalls: It differs from the investor's personal capital return calculated using XIRR.

definition: A group's or position's share of portfolio value.
reading: Weights describe concentration based on available data.
pitfalls: Missing valuations can distort weights; these are not target allocations.

definition: The currency in which an instrument's price is quoted.
reading: Converting its valuation to PLN requires the appropriate exchange rate.
pitfalls: The listing currency does not describe a company's or ETF's full currency exposure.

definition: The value of held units at available prices and exchange rates.
reading: The valuation's source and time show which data produced the result.
pitfalls: A missing quote produces an incomplete valuation, not zero value.

definition: A personal list of instruments to follow.
reading: The user sets the order and notes.
pitfalls: Being on a watchlist does not mean a position is held in the portfolio.

definition: Tax withheld from a payment, such as a foreign dividend.
reading: The net amount reflects this deduction.
pitfalls: It does not settle all of the investor's tax obligations.

definition: An instrument's value change adjusted for flows assigned to it that day.
reading: The percentage contribution uses the same portfolio basis as daily P/L.
pitfalls: The residual includes cash and events not assigned to instruments; data gaps remain explicit.

definition: The number of instrument units that changed hands during an interval.
reading: Volume describes trading activity.
pitfalls: High volume alone does not determine the direction of the next price change.

definition: The value change since the previous close, less the day's external flows.
reading: A deposit is not treated as a gain.
pitfalls: Incomplete prices or exchange rates can limit result completeness.

definition: The difference between current position value and acquisition cost in the instrument currency.
reading: Compare amounts only in the same currency.
pitfalls: PLN P/L also depends on exchange rates.

definition: The difference between proceeds and the cost of consumed FIFO lots during a period.
reading: Economic and tax views may use different exchange rates and costs.
pitfalls: Informational results do not replace tax reporting; unknown costs are excluded from totals.

definition: A rate of return accounting for the amounts and dates of cash flows.
reading: It also depends on when deposits and withdrawals occur.
pitfalls: Some cash flows do not produce a unique result.

definition: The lowest and highest available prices over the last 52 weeks.
reading: The range describes the instrument's observed history.
pitfalls: Historical bounds do not constrain future prices. Incomplete history can narrow the range.

definition: An instrument-related event, such as a split or dividend.
reading: It explains some changes in unit count or price.
pitfalls: A missing event in the data can distort analysis.

definition: The price difference from the previous close, in amount and percentage.
reading: The percentage uses the previous closing price as its base.
pitfalls: It is not your portfolio's P/L; it does not account for quantity, costs or flows.
